title: Hoop vs Disk: Why a Disk Wins
topic: Rolling without slipping — energy conservation gives v = √(2gh / (1 + I/MR²)); disk beats hoop because less inertia goes into rotation

beats.narration: Two wheels — same mass, same radius, same hill. Which one reaches the bottom first?

elements.content: Two wheels, same mass, same radius — which one wins?

beats.narration: We release a hoop and a solid disk from rest at the top of an inclined ramp. Both roll without slipping.

h (height label with bracket on left side)
Hoop: ring outline at top of ramp, amber stroke
elements.position: upper hoop, slightly above ramp surface

Disk: filled solid circle at top of ramp, rose stroke

elements.content: I = ½MR² label next to disk

beats.narration: By energy conservation, the gravitational potential energy m g h becomes kinetic energy — split between translation, one half m v squared, and rotation, one half I omega squared.
Plug in: for the disk, v equals the square root of four g h divided by three. For the hoop, v equals the square root of g h. The disk is always faster — about fifteen percent quicker at the bottom.
Less rotational inertia leaves more energy for translation — that's why a solid disk beats a hoop.

elements.content: Less rotational inertia → more translational speed.
